transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, what finally brought me in today is that... I just feel like the part of me that used to reach out to people and actually take pleasure in things has gone very quiet. 

I used to really enjoy my work, doing yoga, going to galleries, even just journaling at home. But lately, it feels like I’m mostly just moving through my obligations. I do what I have to do every day, but that connection or enjoyment is just missing.
How long have you been feeling this way—this loss of enjoyment and the sense of just going through the motions?

It's been... about eight months now. This whole change in how I'm thinking, how I approach my work, and just connecting with people—it all started around the time we moved my older relative into our apartment. Ever since then, it's just been going on like this.
Before your relative moved in eight months ago, were you experiencing any of these feelings—like low mood, loss of interest in things, or difficulty enjoying activities—even occasionally?

No... no, I really wasn't. I mean, before that point, I was doing fine. I had normal stress from work, sure, but I didn't have this... this low mood or trouble enjoying things. I was still very much engaged with my life and the things I liked doing. It really just seemed to start right around the time they moved in.

When your relative first moved in eight months ago, did your mood and enjoyment of activities drop quite suddenly—like within days or a week or two—or was it more of a gradual decline over several weeks?

It was... well, it wasn't overnight. I'd say it was more of a gradual thing. At first, it was just the stress of the adjustment, you know, having someone new in the space. But then over the course of a few weeks, I just sort of realized that I wasn't wanting to do the things I usually do. The enjoyment just slowly faded out.
Over these past eight months, have you noticed changes in your sleep—like sleeping more or less than usual—or changes in your appetite?

Um... no, not really. I mean, my sleep is pretty much the same as it's always been. I get up and go to sleep around the same times. And my appetite... I haven't noticed any big changes there either. I'm still eating my regular meals. So, no, nothing like that.

Over these eight months, have there been times when you felt a bit better or had moments where you enjoyed something—perhaps when you were away from home or doing something unrelated to your relative being there—or has this low mood and loss of enjoyment been pretty constant regardless of what's happening around you?

Well... honestly, it's been pretty constant. I haven't really had any moments where I felt better or found myself enjoying things, even if I'm out of the house or at work. It doesn't seem to matter where I am or what I'm doing, that low feeling just... it just stays with me all the time.
Over these past eight months, have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for how you're feeling, or for things related to your relative moving in?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I know it's a difficult situation with them moving in, but I haven't really felt guilty about it. It's just... it is what it is. I don't blame myself for feeling this way, it just sort of happened. So, no, no guilt or anything like that.
If your relative were to move out tomorrow, do you think your mood and your ability to enjoy things would likely improve, or do you think you'd still feel this way regardless?

I don't really know. I mean, it's hard to imagine them just leaving tomorrow. But honestly... considering how constant this feeling has been, I kind of think I'd still feel this way even if they did. It doesn't feel like it's just about them being in the house anymore. It just feels like this is how things are now.

Over these past eight months, have you found yourself feeling worthless or like you're not good enough—or have you been very critical of yourself in ways that feel different from how you normally are?

No, I haven't really felt worthless or anything like that. I mean, I'm just tired and down, but I don't feel like I'm not good enough or... or overly critical of myself. I know I'm still capable of doing my job and everything, it's just that I don't get any joy out of it right now. So, no, my self-worth hasn't really been an issue.

Over these past eight months, have you noticed changes in how you move or act—like feeling physically slowed down, moving more slowly than usual, or conversely, feeling restless or fidgety in a way that's different from your normal self?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't feel like I'm moving in slow motion or anything, and I'm not... I'm not pacing around or feeling restless either. My energy is just low, but my actual movements feel normal, I guess. I haven't felt any physical changes like that.
Have you ever experienced periods—even briefly—where your mood was unusually high or elevated, where you had a lot of energy, or where you needed much less sleep than normal but still felt rested?

No, I haven't had anything like that. I've never really been the type to have a lot of energy or feel unusually high. And I definitely need my sleep. If I don't get enough, I feel it. So no, I've never had a period where I felt like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for Major Depressive Disorder, single episode. She presents with persistent depressed mood and anhedonia (loss of interest/pleasure in previously enjoyed activities) for 8 months. While the onset was temporally related to a psychosocial stressor (relative moving in), the depression has become independent of the stressor and persists constantly regardless of circumstance. Absence of manic/hypomanic episodes rules out bipolar disorder. The duration, severity, and functional impairment (going through obligations without enjoyment) exceed what would be expected for an adjustment disorder, though F43.21 remains a differential consideration given the clear stressor.
